overlaps.original: How Stripe's Product and Price objects model a business catalog. Core resources for Checkout, Payment Links, Subscriptions, Invoices, and Quotes integrations.

suggestions.replacement: Products define what a business sells. Prices define how much and how often the business charges. These objects support Checkout, Payment Links, Subscriptions, Invoices and Quotes.

The April 20 and [November 7, 2026 catalog overviews](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/how-products-and-prices-work) explain how [[stripe]] Products describe goods and services and Prices specify amounts, currencies, billing intervals, and tax behavior. Merchants can create them in the Dashboard or import a catalog using the Products and Prices APIs for Checkout, Payment Links, Subscriptions, Invoices, and Quotes.

overlaps.original:
- **Custom product IDs** — unlike most Stripe resources, you can choose your own product ID (use internal system IDs for easy reconciliation)
- **Prices are immutable** — never modify `unit_amount`; archive (`active: false`) and create new price instead
- **`price_data`** — creates temporary Price objects invisible in Dashboard catalog; use for dynamic amounts (e.g. donations); Product objects may persist
- **Max recurring interval**: 3 years
- **Subscription constraint**: all prices must share same `recurring.interval` + `recurring.interval_count` (unless flexible billing mode)
- **Archive not delete**: products/prices can't be deleted in general; only archive; Stripe stores indefinitely for transaction history

suggestions.replacement: ## Product and Price lifecycle

- **Custom Product IDs** — a merchant can choose a Product ID, including an ID from its own catalog.
- **Catalog design** — November recommends one Product for each distinct customer-facing option, entitlement, tax code, or separately displayed item. For the same Product, use Prices for different intervals or currencies and a replacement Price when the amount changes. The Starter, Professional, and Enterprise example uses three Products with monthly and annual Prices for each. Checkout, Payment Links, and invoices display the Product name per line item. Items sharing a Product also share its name and description.
- **Change amounts** — create a new Price and archive the old one using `active: false`. Stripe preserves historical transaction records. The separate April management guide describes updating Price `metadata`, `nickname`, and `active`.
- **Inline `price_data`** — create inline prices through the API for a specific Checkout Session, Payment Link, Subscription, or invoice. These Prices stay out of Dashboard catalog listings and searches but can be viewed by direct Dashboard URL. Related Products can persist. The April management guide says inline Prices are effectively archived by default and cannot be updated or reused.
- **Subscription limits** — the maximum recurrence is three years. Outside flexible billing for mixed intervals, all Prices on a Subscription must share both `recurring.interval` and `recurring.interval_count`.
- **Archive or delete** — both overviews prefer archival to preserve history and describe Dashboard deletion exceptions for a never-used Price or a Product without Prices. The separate April manage guide also documents Product deletion and its associated-Price limits.

| | Product | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defines | What you sell | How much + how often |

suggestions.replacement: ## Price types

| Defines | What you sell | How much and how often |
| ID | Merchant may choose an ID | Stripe-generated |
| Creation | Name required | Currency and Product association, with amount parameters depending on billing scheme |
| Other fields | Description, image, tax code, and the optional `default_price` pointing to a Price | Recurring fields for recurring Prices. When calculating taxes, `tax_behavior` is required if no default is configured in Stripe Tax. An explicit `inclusive` or `exclusive` value cannot be changed. |

For `POST /v1/prices`, pass an existing Product ID via `product` or create the related Product with `product_data.name`, as shown in the November Invoice Items API example's `createPrice` prerequisite. For non-tiered Prices, the November Prices API reference requires one of `unit_amount`, `unit_amount_decimal`, or `custom_unit_amount`. Tiered Prices use `billing_scheme=tiered`, `tiers`, and `tiers_mode`. Set or change the default Price on the Product.

The April overview says it is absent from the main Dashboard catalog but viewable directly, and associated Product objects may persist. |

| Recurring | Subscription billing with a recurrence interval |
| Inline (`price_data`) | API-created for a specific resource and excluded from Dashboard catalog listings |

| Multi-currency | One Price can offer amounts in multiple currencies |

When the merchant explicitly passes amount and currency for an API invoice item or charge, Stripe uses those values. The November catalog overview assigns the choice of localized amount and currency to the merchant in these cases. It recommends `pricing.price` to pass a Price ID for invoice items. Automatic localization is unverified across Price-ID routes.

overlaps.original:
**Disallowed** = cannot use that product/price with this API at all.
**Ignored** = feature has no effect but product/price still usable.

suggestions.replacement:
**Disallowed** means the feature precludes using that Product or Price with the listed API. **Ignored** means the feature has no effect and the Product or Price remains usable.

The separate November 7 Payment Links create guide lists flat-rate or tiered pricing for recurring products and flat-rate or package pricing for one-off products. Its tiered wording conflicts with the two catalog tables. Its flat-rate request examples document the creation routes below and leave exact tiered support by route, subtype, and version unresolved. They do not establish general support for metering, decimal amounts, or all package combinations. See [[stripe-payment-links]].

The overview uses **Disallowed** where the Product or Price cannot be used with the API, and **Ignored** where the resource is usable but the feature has no effect. The April and November management guides document an explicit invoice-item currency path below.

overlaps.original:
- **Checkout**: specify price `id` per line item; renders product name + image
- **Payment Links**: Dashboard-created; renders product name + image
- **Subscriptions**: price must be recurring; billing period = `recurring.interval`; multiple prices OK if same interval
- **Quotes**: models one-off invoice or subscription; auto-creates invoices/subscriptions on acceptance
- **Invoices**: specify price `id` per line item; uses `product.name` in invoice PDF

suggestions.replacement:
- **Checkout** — specify a Price ID per line item or use inline `price_data`. The Session computes totals and shows the Product name and image.
- **Payment Links** — create the link in the Dashboard or use `POST /v1/payment_links`. The November create guide demonstrates `line_items[][price]` for an existing Price ID or `line_items[][price_data]` with `product_data` to create a Product and Price inline. Both examples include a quantity. The link computes totals and shows the Product name and image.
- **Subscriptions** — use recurring Prices. Outside flexible billing the intervals and counts have to match. The separate May mixed-interval guide describes flexible billing, interval alignment, and API version requirements. The November mixed-interval selector routes to Dashboard and API variants. See [[stripe-subscriptions]] and [[stripe-subscriptions-mixed-interval]].
- **Quotes** — specify a Price ID for a one-off invoice or subscription. On customer acceptance Stripe creates the relevant billing objects. Acceptance does not establish collection.
- **Invoices** — a Price ID can identify the line item's Price. Stripe uses `product.name` when rendering the invoice on the web or as a PDF. The separate November Invoice Items API reference also documents inline `price_data` and the explicit amount and currency fields.

- **Checkout.** Supply each line-item Price ID. Checkout renders the Product name and image. The management guides describe selecting a supported local currency based on IP, with default-currency fallback and an explicit `currency` option. Applicable Prices, coupons, promotion codes and shipping rates in a Session must share a default currency and all support the local currency for automatic selection.
- **Payment Links.** Create a link from the catalog. It renders the Product name and image. The guide describes local-currency selection when all included Prices support it, default fallback, and a `currency` override. The Prices must share a default currency.
- **Subscriptions.** Use recurring prices. The April overview sets a three-year maximum interval and requires matching `recurring.interval` and `recurring.interval_count` unless flexible billing mode is used to support mixed intervals. Checkout uses its currency-selection flow. For directly created subscriptions, pass `currency` to select a nondefault option. Subscription schedules use `phases.currency` and otherwise follow the Price default.
- **Quotes.** Use a Price ID or select a Product in the Dashboard. Accepted quotes can create the associated invoice or subscription. The management guides say Quotes use the Price’s default currency.
- **Invoices.** Use the Price ID for API invoice items. The invoice uses the Product name in the PDF. When selecting a multi-currency Price’s currency for an invoice item, explicitly pass `currency` even if it matches the Customer default. The management guides say omitting the parameter prevents this multi-currency path from working.

## Catalog operations and tests

- **Lookup keys.** Retrieve Prices by `lookup_key`. To publish a replacement amount under the same lookup key, create a Price with `transfer_lookup_key=true`. Expand `currency_options` to retrieve currency-specific amounts.
- **Rounding.** For decimal pricing, the management guides round invoice line items after multiplying unit amount by quantity, before summing. They separately distinguish invoice-level automatic tax rounding from configurable manual tax rounding.
- **Import synchronization.** Map your Product IDs, keep Stripe Price IDs and compare current amounts. The guide’s one-active-Price convention applies to this example synchronization pattern. If the amount differs, create a replacement Price and make the old one inactive.
- **Dashboard copy to live.** The April management guide says a test Product can be copied once. The November guide says the same sandbox Product can be copied repeatedly from the Dashboard. Associated Prices copy and each copy creates a separate live Product. On both dates, later test or sandbox edits do not propagate to existing live copies.

## Detail locators

- November management lines 18–170 and 422–500 cover Product and Price creation, archival, deletion and updates. Lines 232–275 cover defaults and inline Prices.
- November management lines 277–409 cover currency options, product-specific selection, lookup keys and rounding. Lines 506–557 cover import and synchronization. November lines 591–595 and April management lines 697–701 record the dated Dashboard copy rules.
- April catalog overview lines 63–75 cover inline Price visibility. Lines 109–137 cover compatibility and recurring interval limits.

overlaps.original: Overview of the Account Signals API for Connect platforms: 3 webhook-driven signal types for connected account risk, triggering actions via Radar for Platforms.

suggestions.replacement: The Account Signals API supplies risk intelligence for Connect platforms about potential merchant fraud, financial distress and website legitimacy. The platform can review a signal and choose an account action in Radar. See the dated contract for each signal.

The May 10 and November 7, 2026 captures of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/account-risk-signals describe programmatic risk signals for Connect platforms. Stripe evaluates connected-account activity and sends a webhook when a risk signal changes. The May guide lists three signal types. November adds payment delinquency exposure and illustrates the platform retrieving the signal and deciding how to respond.

[[stripe|Stripe]] Account Signals provides risk intelligence for Connect platforms across fraudulent merchant, merchant delinquency, and fraudulent website signals. Website evaluation is on demand, including for a prospective business.

[[stripe|Stripe]] Account Signals provides risk intelligence for Connect platforms. A signal's readiness and a platform operator's choice to take action are separate. The November delinquency guide specifies the risk of carrying a negative balance for more than 90 days.

overlaps.original:
| Signal | Detects | Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fraudulent merchant | Misrepresentation, unauthorized transactions, first-party fraud | ML model (continuous) |
| Merchant delinquency risk | Financial distress → unfulfilled orders, disputes, negative balances | ML model (continuous) |
| Fraudulent website | Deceptive/policy-violating websites, fake storefronts | On-demand analysis |

suggestions.replacement:
| Signal | Documented scope |
| --- | --- |
| Fraudulent merchant | Risk indicators such as misrepresentation, unauthorized transactions or first-party fraud. Stripe evaluates account activity. |
| Merchant delinquency risk | Financial distress associated with potential unfulfilled orders, disputes, refunds or negative balances. |
| Fraudulent website | On-demand evaluation for deceptive or policy-violating websites, including misleading claims or fake storefronts. |
| Payment delinquency exposure | Added to the November overview. Estimates dollars at risk from potential disputes and refunds if a connected account becomes delinquent. |
| Fraudulent merchant | Misrepresentation, unauthorized transactions, first-party fraud | Stripe evaluates new and existing connected accounts automatically |
| Merchant delinquency risk | May describes financial distress. November specifies risk of carrying a negative balance for more than 90 days. | Risk assessment for a connected account |

overlaps.original: Signal changes trigger webhook events to your endpoint.

suggestions.replacement: November says account signals and account evaluations can be retrieved for up to 90 days after creation. List requests omit account signals created more than 90 days ago. The overview states a retrieval and list boundary. The separate delinquency-risk guide's negative balance lasting more than 90 days describes the risk being assessed. [[raw/stripe-radar-merchant-delinquency-risk-2026-11-07|November delinquency risk detail, lines 8–13]]
Readiness or creation events and their payloads are signal-specific. The November fraudulent-merchant guide describes a notification when Stripe creates that signal.

The May account-risk overview describes continuous evaluation with signal-change notifications. It separately labels the website signal on demand. The November delinquency guide below describes a readiness event after evaluation. Choose any platform action separately.

The May account-risk overview describes continuous evaluation with signal-change notifications. It separately labels the website signal on demand. The November website guide below describes website evaluation readiness events for that route.

overlaps.original: Raise review, pause payouts, pause payments, reject account, set reserves, request identity verification — all via Radar for Platforms.

suggestions.replacement: Available Radar actions for existing connected accounts include raising a review, pausing payouts or payments, rejecting the account, setting reserves, and requesting identity verification when eligible. The website evaluation provides a result for the platform to assess.

May links to the [Core event-types route for `2026-03-25.preview`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/events/event-types.md?api-version=2026-03-25.preview). November links to the [Account Signals API with `api-version=preview`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/signals/account-signals.md?api-version=preview). Its diagram shows connected-account payments or disputes feeding Stripe's models, a signal-ready webhook to the platform backend, retrieval by `GET /v2/signals/account_signals/{id}`, and the platform receiving signal level and indicators before deciding whether to review, pause or reject. The notification signals readiness. The November fraudulent merchant and fraudulent website detail guides specify thin events. The separate merchant delinquency risk and payment delinquency exposure guides describe when readiness notifications are sent and leave those event bodies unspecified.

May's Radar for Platforms action table lists raising a review, pausing payouts, pausing payments, rejecting a confirmed fraudulent account, setting reserves and requesting identity verification. November replaces the table with a route to account fraud prevention. That guide retains the six options, qualifies request identity verification on use of Stripe Identity, directs platforms to Stripe Support to reverse rejection, and names Connect Risk Analyst, Administrator or Super Administrator for risk reviews. These are platform decisions. A signal is an input to that decision and leaves confirmed fraud and action execution unverified. [[source-stripe-radar-for-platforms|Radar for Platforms]] · [[raw/stripe-radar-account-fraud-prevention-2026-11-07|November account fraud prevention, lines 102–126, 140–154 and 162–166]]

## Separately captured November signal details

- **Fraudulent merchant.** The ready event is thin with an empty `data` object. Retrieve the signal using `related_object.id`. The detail guide lists the signal from Radar Standard upward and the returned 0–100 probability only on Plus and Pro. The earlier detailed capture below describes a payload with full details. [[raw/stripe-radar-fraudulent-merchant-2026-11-07|November fraudulent merchant detail, lines 9–24 and 43–51]]
- **Merchant delinquency risk.** The detail names `v2.signals.account_signal.merchant_delinquency_ready`, compared with the earlier v1 event below, and gives an early-access request. [[raw/stripe-radar-merchant-delinquency-risk-2026-11-07|November delinquency risk detail, lines 8–13 and 60–66]]
- **Fraudulent website.** On-demand evaluation uses `POST /v2/signals/account_evaluations`, compared with the earlier Core endpoint below. The individual ready event `v2.signals.account_signal.fraudulent_website_ready` and optional `v2.signals.account_evaluation.complete` for multiple signals are thin. Use `related_object.id` to retrieve the resource. The detail allows sandbox testing on any Radar plan and specifies Plus or Pro with 4,000 monthly requests for live use. [[raw/stripe-radar-fraudulent-website-2026-11-07|November fraudulent website detail, lines 9–26 and 63–73]]
- **Payment delinquency exposure.** The separate guide describes requesting early access and lists `v2.signals.account_signal.payment_delinquency_exposure_ready`. Its conditional monetary estimate is a separate signal from merchant delinquency risk. [[raw/stripe-radar-payment-delinquency-exposure-2026-11-07|November payment delinquency exposure, lines 7–13 and 55–61]]

The overview's diagram and these child guides leave account-specific entitlement and common delivery semantics across signal types unresolved.
**Risk levels in the separate May 10, 2026 delinquency guide**: `highest`, `elevated`, `normal`, `low`, `not_assessed`.

The May 10 and November 7, 2026 captures at [Merchant delinquency risk](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/merchant-delinquency-risk) describe a Connect platform retrieving Stripe's latest delinquency evaluation, with a risk level and indicators for the connected account. The November guide defines the prediction as risk of carrying a negative balance for more than 90 days. It gives disputes, refunds and failed payouts as examples of events that can contribute to unrecoverable balances. The 90 days is a prediction horizon. The guide describes an email request for early access. Individual access and whether an account is currently delinquent remain separate.
